edges.paper_title: Effect of additive acid on seeded growth of gold nanobipyramids
edges.parameter_range: 0 to 1 mL
edges.mechanism: Addition of acid alters the reduction kinetics of gold ions and modulates the surface passivation by halide/anions on specific crystallographic facets during seeded growth.
edges.quantitative_effect: Yield ranges from 5.21 ± 0.44% to 91.46 ± 3.32%
edges.evidence_quote: Morphological characterization shows the nanoseeds that were grown in growth solution prepared using HCl, H2SO4, and HF at concentration from 0 to 1 mL produced GNBPs with yield ranges from 5.21 ± 0.44 to 91.46 ± 3.32%

edges.paper_title: Effect of additive acid on seeded growth of gold nanobipyramids
edges.parameter_range: 0 to 1 mL
edges.mechanism: Changes in proton concentration and anion complexation modify the relative growth rates of tips versus equatorial facets, tuning the axial elongation.
edges.quantitative_effect: Aspect ratio increases from 2.00 ± 0.02 to 2.76 ± 0.05
edges.evidence_quote: aspect ratio from 2.00 ± 0.02 to 2.76 ± 0.05

edges.paper_title: Design and synthesis of gold nanostars-based SERS nanotags for bioimaging applications
edges.parameter_range: Core-shell and nanostar engineering parameters
edges.mechanism: Rational tailoring of plasmonic core morphology and electromagnetic field enhancement zones optimizes signal intensity and specificity for SERS detection.
edges.quantitative_effect: Achieves high signal intensity and tunable fingerprint-like SERS spectra.
edges.evidence_quote: Design parameters include fine-tuning the properties of the plasmonic core as well as optimizing the choice of Raman reporter molecule, surface coating, and targeting moieties

edges.paper_title: Shape tunable synthesis of anisotropic gold nanostructures through binary surfactant mixtures
edges.parameter_range: Binary CTAB/DDAB surfactant mixtures
edges.mechanism: Engineering the binary surfactant mixture modifies the mixed micelle soft-template geometry and interfacial packing, which directs anisotropic growth toward bipyramidal and related elongated nanostructures.
edges.quantitative_effect: Significant improvement in the yield of Au bipyramidal type nanoparticles without shape selection procedures.
edges.evidence_quote: The results showed significant improvement in the yield of Au bipyramidal type nanoparticles in different sizes (nm to mm) by using binary surfactant mixtures without any need for shape selection procedure.

edges.paper_title: Shape tunable synthesis of anisotropic gold nanostructures through binary surfactant mixtures
edges.parameter_range: Varied pH in binary surfactant mixture
edges.mechanism: Altering the solution pH modifies the redox potential of ascorbic acid and the protonation/interaction state of the surfactant headgroups and stabilizing ions at the nanoparticle surface.
edges.quantitative_effect: Controlled shape transitions between truncated bipyramids, dogbones, and nanodumbbells.
edges.evidence_quote: By varying the pH and concentration of ascorbic acid, we can control the shape and size of Au nanoparticles (i.e., truncated bipyramids, dogbones, and nanodumbbells) at fixed CTAB/DDAB ratios.

edges.paper_title: Highly improved synthesis of gold nanobipyramids by tuning the concentration of hydrochloric acid
edges.parameter_range: Systematically varied HCl concentration
edges.mechanism: Abundant HCl slows down the reduction rate and modulates chloride/bromide ion adsorption on crystal faces, enhancing the formation yield of gold nanobipyramids.
edges.quantitative_effect: Abundant HCl significantly improves the yield of Au BPs.
edges.evidence_quote: The results showed that the abundant HCl could improve the yield of Au BPs and decrease the longitudinal surface plasmon resonance wavelength

edges.paper_title: Twinned Gold Nanoparticles under Growth: Bipyramids Shape Controlled by Environment
edges.parameter_range: Addition of 0.01 M HCl
edges.mechanism: Addition of HCl modifies solution pH and chloride complexation, further slowing reduction kinetics and promoting pronounced anisotropic elongation of bipyramids.
edges.quantitative_effect: LSPR shifts beyond 850 nm.
edges.evidence_quote: HCl concentration=0.01 M -> morphology=gold nanobipyramids, LSPR=>850 nm

edges.paper_title: Gold Bipyramid Nanoparticle Dimers
edges.parameter_range: 100 µL of 30 mM HCl yielding final pH 3
edges.mechanism: Adjusting pH and proton concentration controls the surface charge and electrostatic stabilization of gold nanobipyramids, enabling targeted tip-to-tip and bowtie dimer assembly via zwitterionic amino acid linkers.
edges.quantitative_effect: Assembled bowtie dimers exhibit a ~20% red shift in plasmon resonance (LSPR reaches 969 nm).
edges.evidence_quote: In the bowtie orientation, the dimers exhibit a 20% red shift in their plasmon resonance as compared to the individual particles ... LSPR=969

edges.paper_title: Highly improved synthesis of gold nanobipyramids by tuning the concentration of hydrochloric acid
edges.parameter_range: Systematically varied HCl concentration
edges.mechanism: Increased proton and chloride levels alter the growth kinetics and relative facets growth rates, leading to a blue-shift in the optical absorption.
edges.quantitative_effect: Decreases the longitudinal surface plasmon resonance wavelength.
edges.evidence_quote: decrease the longitudinal surface plasmon resonance wavelength

edges.paper_title: Production of Monodisperse Gold Nanobipyramids with Number Percentages Approaching 100% and Evaluation of Their Plasmonic Properties
edges.parameter_range: From 0.093 mM to higher growth modifications
edges.mechanism: Higher silver ion concentrations promote underpotential deposition (UPD) of Ag on specific facets, enhancing anisotropic growth and shifting longitudinal localized surface plasmon resonance.
edges.quantitative_effect: LSPR peak red-shifts from 690 nm to 833 nm and 914 nm with adjusted reagent sets.
edges.evidence_quote: Ensemble LSPR peak at 690 nm ... LSPR 833 nm ... LSPR 914 nm

edges.paper_title: Beyond the Concentration Limitation in the Synthesis of Nanobipyramids and Other Pentatwinned Gold Nanostructures
edges.parameter_range: 20 µL to 60 µL of 40 mM AgNO3
edges.mechanism: Adjusting silver ion levels during the high-concentration Growth-to-Seed (GtS) slow addition modulates facet passivation and side-growth kinetics, enabling precise control over the final aspect ratio at scale.
edges.quantitative_effect: Aspect ratio increases from 1.96 (length 45 nm, width 23 nm) to 4.19 (length 155 nm, width 37 nm).
edges.evidence_quote: AgNO3 volume (seed vial + growth vial)=20 µL + 24 µL ... AR=1.96 ... AgNO3 volume (seed vial + growth vial)=20 µL + 60 µL ... AR=4.19

edges.paper_title: Twinned Gold Nanoparticles under Growth: Bipyramids Shape Controlled by Environment
edges.parameter_range: 0.045 mM to 0.14 mM
edges.mechanism: Higher AgNO3 concentrations enhance Ag+ underpotential deposition on side facets, stabilizing multitwinned decahedral and bipyramidal structures against isotropic broadening.
edges.quantitative_effect: Aspect ratio increases; LSPR shifts to ~680 nm with 0.14 mM AgNO3 compared to reference conditions.
edges.evidence_quote: AgNO3 concentration=0.14 mM -> morphology=gold nanobipyramids with higher aspect ratio ... LSPR=~680 nm

edges.paper_id: Advanced Optical Materials - 2015 - Li - Production of Monodisperse Gold Nanobipyramids with Number Percentages Approaching
edges.paper_title: Production of Monodisperse Gold Nanobipyramids with Number Percentages Approaching 100% and Evaluation of Their Plasmonic Properties
edges.parameter_range: 0.4 mL down to 0.2 mL in 40 mL growth solution
edges.mechanism: Decreasing the seed-to-metal precursor ratio increases the amount of available gold and silver growth monomer per seed particle, resulting in larger final particle dimensions.
edges.quantitative_effect: Length increases from 49 ± 3 nm (with 0.4 mL seed) to 117 ± 9 nm (with 0.2 mL seed).
edges.evidence_quote: tip-to-tip length 49 nm ... tip-to-tip length 117 nm

edges.paper_title: High-Yield Seeded Growth of Monodisperse Pentatwinned Gold Nanoparticles through Thermally Induced Seed Twinning
edges.parameter_range: Thermal treatment at 80 °C for 90 min
boundary_conditions: Seeded growth of pentatwinned gold nanoparticles
edges.mechanism: Thermal treatment of small gold seeds induces extensive structural reorganization and twinning, creating a high population of pentatwinned seeds that act as templates for preferential bipyramidal growth.
edges.quantitative_effect: Drastic improvement in the yield of pentatwinned nanoparticles exceeding 85%.
edges.evidence_quote: We show that thermal treatment of small Au seeds results in extensive twinning and a subsequent drastic improvement in the yield (>85%) of formation of pentatwinned nanoparticles

edges.paper_title: Size-controlled synthesis of gold bipyramids using an aqueous mixture of CTAC and salicylate anions as the soft template
edges.parameter_range: Varying amounts of salicylate anions (Sal-) added to CTAC
edges.mechanism: Salicylate ions intercalate into CTAC micelles to form rod-shaped mixed micelles, which serve as tailored soft templates governing the anisotropic one-dimensional growth of gold bipyramids.
edges.quantitative_effect: Length and optical properties of the synthesized Au bipyramids are controlled with precision by varying the amount of salicylate anions.
edges.evidence_quote: The length and optical properties of the synthesized Au bipyramids are controlled with precision by varying the amount of salicylate anions (Sal-) added during the synthesis.

edges.paper_title: From gold nanobipyramids to nanojavelins for a precise tuning of the plasmon resonance to the infrared wavelengths: experimental and theoretical aspects
edges.parameter_range: Varied 8-HQL reducing system in CTAB/CTAC mixtures
edges.mechanism: Using 8-hydroxyquinoline as a milder reducing agent alongside CTAC/CTAB mixtures slows down the reduction rate of Au(III) to Au(I)/Au(0), facilitating extreme anisotropic overgrowth into elongated nanojavelins.
edges.quantitative_effect: Tunable aspect ratios extending to very high values for precise infrared plasmon tuning.
edges.evidence_quote: From gold nanobipyramids to nanojavelins for a precise tuning of the plasmon resonance to the infrared wavelengths

edges.paper_title: On the origin of controlled anisotropic growth of monodisperse gold nanobipyramids
edges.parameter_range: 0.045 M down to 0.011 M
edges.mechanism: Lowering CTAB concentration alters the surfactant bilayer coverage and bromide counterion adsorption on distinct gold crystallographic facets, disrupting the delicate side-facet passivation required for uniform bipyramidal growth.
edges.quantitative_effect: Decreasing CTAB from 0.045 M to 0.022 M and 0.011 M results in elongated/distorted GNBs mixed with small nanorods, spheres, and polydisperse structures.
edges.evidence_quote: run_ctab_0.022M: morphology=elongated and distorted gold nanobipyramids mixed with small nanorods and spheres ... run_ctab_0.011M: morphology=polydisperse elongated gold nanorods and particles

edges.paper_title: Optimization of the Surfactant Ratio in the Formation of Penta-Twinned Seeds for Precision Synthesis of Gold Nanobipyramids with Tunable Plasmon Resonances
edges.raw_parameter: CTAC to sodium citrate molar ratio in seed solution
edges.parameter_range: Optimized binary CTAC/sodium citrate surfactant ratio
edges.mechanism: Tuning the molar ratio between CTAC and sodium citrate in the seed growth mixture optimizes the formation and stability of penta-twinned seeds, eliminating impurity byproducts and ensuring monodispersity.
edges.quantitative_effect: Precision synthesis of high-purity gold nanobipyramids with narrow size distribution and tunable plasmon resonances.
edges.evidence_quote: Optimization of the Surfactant Ratio in the Formation of Penta-Twinned Seeds for Precision Synthesis of Gold Nanobipyramids with Tunable Plasmon Resonances

edges.paper_title: Bipyramid-templated synthesis of monodisperse anisotropic gold nanocrystals
edges.parameter_range: Singular CTAB versus binary CTAC/CTAB surfactant systems
edges.mechanism: Binary surfactant combinations and purification via depletion flocculation selectively isolate monodisperse bipyramid cores, which then serve as uniform templates for secondary anisotropic overgrowth or oxidative etching.
edges.quantitative_effect: Enables generation of diverse, highly monodisperse anisotropic gold nanoparticle shapes in high yield.
edges.evidence_quote: Here we show a method to generate diverse and monodisperse anisotropic gold nanoparticle shapes with various tip geometries as well as highly tunable size augmentations

edges.paper_title: Plasmonic Photothermal Gold Bipyramid Nanoreactors for Ultrafast Real-Time Bioassays
edges.parameter_range: Standard 50 rpm vs high stirring rate
boundary_conditions: 500 µL purified gold nanobipyramids in 1 mM CTAB
edges.mechanism: Excessive mechanical agitation during silica shell condensation disrupts uniform hydrolysis and deposition kinetics of TEOS around the bipyramid tips and facets.
edges.quantitative_effect: High stirring yielded irregular silica-coated gold nanobipyramids with tip-exposed structures instead of uniform conformal shells.
edges.evidence_quote: PEG-Si-AuBP_high_stirring: morphology=irregular silica-coated gold nanobipyramids with tip-exposed structures

edges.paper_title: The Many "Facets" of Halide Ions in the Chemistry of Colloidal Inorganic Nanocrystals.
edges.parameter_range: Chloride, bromide, and iodide ions across nanocrystal syntheses
edges.mechanism: Halide ions selectively adsorb onto specific crystal facets and form complexes with metal precursors, regulating surface energy and anisotropic growth kinetics.
edges.quantitative_effect: Provides high level of shape and compositional control in colloidal nanomaterials.
edges.evidence_quote: Halide ions affect the NC growth kinetics through several means, including selective binding on crystal facets, complexation with the precursors, and oxidative etching.

edges.paper_title: Seed-Mediated Synthesis of Thin Gold Nanoplates with Tunable Edge Lengths and Optical Properties
edges.parameter_range: Sulfite ligand in Au-Ag alloy nanoframes seed-mediated synthesis
edges.mechanism: Sulfite ligands complex effectively with Au(III) precursor ions to regulate reduction kinetics and govern the anisotropic growth of thin nanoplates.
edges.quantitative_effect: Edge lengths tunable from 48 nm to 167 nm.
edges.evidence_quote: run_thin_nanoplates_range: morphology=thin gold nanoplates, L=48–167 nm, W=7.5 nm
